AI Agents 2026-11-18

⬛ Overview · 🟪 AI Agents · 🟦 AI Models & Labs · 🟧 AI Policy · 🟨 Data Engineering

Projects: 15 | Active today: 5 | Stable releases: 9 | Prereleases (not covered): 5 | Generated: 2026-11-18 07:08 UTC

Highlights

  • socket.dev reports that compromised versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 of Microsoft's agent-framework PyPI package use .pth startup hooks to exfiltrate Azure, GitHub Actions, and CI/CD credentials.
  • Oh My Pi v18.22.1–v18.22.2 carries a breaking change: the JavaScript eval commit helper now validates its arguments strictly, throwing a TypeError on unknown option names or non-object options.
  • A Harvard study says AI coding agents increased code production by 30%, while completed work did not measurably rise and review time grew by 49%.

Coding Agents & Assistants

Claude Code

  • Release: v2.1.327 fixes several data-loss and safety bugs: stopping a Remote Control server in worktree mode no longer deletes a running session's git-ignored files such as .env, self-hosted runners using --use-anthropic-git-proxy no longer delete a non-empty directory named by GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL, and claude mcp add/claude mcp remove with project scope no longer drop other top-level keys from .mcp.json. It adds a confirmation before /install-github-app changes a repository, a /status listing of broken agent, skill, command and output-style files and other misconfigurations, and /tui classic as the name for the non-fullscreen renderer.
  • News: How the Claude Code team thinks about verification describes how end-to-end, property and differential tests let coding agents verify their work with evidence, and what the Claude Code team does to keep its verifiers honest.

OpenAI Codex

  • Release: rust-v0.169.1–rust-v0.170.0 fixes MCP OAuth credential races during cancellation, login, and logout, keeps child threads and permission updates from losing existing sandbox restrictions, and removes duplicate file search results. It adds WebRTC negotiation for realtime voice calls in the TUI and experimental support for using identically named MCP servers across environments.
  • Hot issue: #57101: An issue reports that on Windows the Codex Computer Use helper and its capture-access record stay open — leaving a gold/yellow border around the display — roughly five hours after a screenshot-producing turn completes, and asks that capture resources be released when their owning work ends. (57 comments, 9 👍; +15 in the last 24h)

OpenCode

  • Release: v1.19.6–v2.3.2 fixes GPT-6.2 models re-billing the system prompt as uncached input on every step and stops sessions with many images from sending oversized requests. Headline additions include timed-out shell commands moving to the background instead of being killed, background compaction now on by default, GPT 6.2 models showing up in the model picker when signing in with ChatGPT, and OpenCode 1 offering an in-app upgrade to OpenCode 2.0.
  • Hot issue: #37216: A feature request asks for i18n support in the TUI, whose strings are hardcoded in English while the app, desktop and console packages already support 17+ locales. (21 comments, 0 👍; +11 in the last 24h)

Oh My Pi

  • Release: v18.22.1–v18.22.2 has a breaking change: the JavaScript eval commit helper now validates its arguments strictly, throwing a TypeError on unknown option names or non-object options, and the obsolete wayland-pipewire Cargo feature and OMP_NATIVE_FEATURES variable are removed. Fixes include no longer feeding failed tool calls back to the model as refusal explanations and OAuth accounts refreshed through an auth broker keeping their stored routing metadata; it also adds a native Kiro provider that signs in with AWS IAM Identity Center, AWS Builder ID, Google, GitHub, or a Kiro API key and reports Kiro credits in /usage.
  • Hot issue: #19578: An issue reports that openai-codex/gpt-6.2-sol and gpt-6.2-astra are missing from OMP's Codex model list after omp models refresh and that a direct request for Sol fails model resolution while the native Codex CLI lists both and completes a Sol request, though the reporter notes the workspace and OMP credential used were not verified. (9 comments, 2 👍; +11 in the last 24h)

Quiet today: Gemini CLI, Kilo Code, Pi, jcode, Cline, Command Code, DeepSeek Harness, Hermes Agent

Agent Tooling

OpenShell

  • Release: v0.1.9 moves the Go SDK to github.com/ai-openshell/sdk-go and deprecates github.com/NVIDIA/OpenShell/sdk/go; wildcard network policy endpoints no longer accept private IP literals alone unless an exact endpoint or allowed_ips grant is present, middleware selectors cannot include a port, and Helm charts with service.metricsPort set to 0 or false fail to render, with metrics.enabled replacing the port value. It also says Postgres gateway migration 010 builds indexes on objects with CREATE INDEX and blocks writes, fixes write-method authorization denial events to report Create, Update, or Delete by class_uid: 6003 and status_id: 2, and includes opt-in HTTP streaming hooks plus mutation_admission_limit_per_caller and mutation_replay_window_seconds controls.

AI Agents 2026-11-17

⬛ Overview · 🟪 AI Agents · 🟦 AI Models & Labs · 🟧 AI Policy · 🟨 Data Engineering

Projects: 15 | Active today: 5 | Stable releases: 7 | Prereleases (not covered): 7 | Generated: 2026-11-17 07:44 UTC

Highlights

  • Oh My Pi v18.21.0–v18.22.0 introduces breaking changes: binary analysis moves to the dsm namespace, ida.* settings are replaced by disassembler.*, legacy standalone disassembler tools and PlanReviewOverlay options are removed, and the AgentSession run lifecycle is reworked with new events and methods (agent_end, agent_pause, isRunActive, wakeSources, waitForRunEnd()).
  • Claude Code hot issue #110480 reports premium seat usage limits (Team/Enterprise) are being exhausted roughly 3–5× faster on non-Fable models (Opus/Sonnet) since the week of November 9, 2026, which the reporter attributes to a metering change rather than workload shifts.
  • jcode v1.0.0 launches jcode Cloud (/cloud moves a session or swarm to a VM, /local brings it back), reworks swarms to plan in phases and parallel lanes with a pinned team progress view, and claims 25% less CPU, idle wakeups down from 2.68 to 1.51/sec, and rendered-span memory in a large conversation down from 20.4 MB to 14.6 MB.

Coding Agents & Assistants

Claude Code

  • Release: v2.1.326 fixes cp being refused when only the file's source was covered by an Edit deny rule, fixes Bash commands that delete or overwrite files (find -delete, cat a > b, sort -o) being summed up in the transcript as a search or a read, fixes a misleading "Dangerous rm operation" warning in the Bash permission prompt on commands with no rm, and fixes background sessions losing the LLM gateway their shell exported — after a crash, a reopen from another folder, or when the background service lacks it — so they now stop before any model request, plus the background service ending the user's own processes, such as an SSH login, when a process number on its list had been reused by another user's process. It also starts sessions with agent teams enabled in Code Mode, warns at startup when a --allowedTools, --disallowedTools or --tools value has an entry that doesn't look like a complete rule, adds a /status row saying when your provider or an environment variable such as DISABLE_TELEMETRY turns features off, and adds OTEL_RESOURCE_INCLUDE_HOST (off by default) to include host.name and host.id in OpenTelemetry resource attributes.
  • News: Tokendoctor – the same Claude Code for up to 38% less — the Hacker News post presents a Claude Code plugin that shows what your use overpays, fixes it with a diff you approve, and puts any change back; it runs on your machine, and the post claims up to 38% lower cost.
  • Hot issue: #110480: an issue reports that premium seat usage limits (Team/Enterprise) are being exhausted roughly 3–5x faster on non-Fable models (Opus / Sonnet) since the week of November 9, 2026, and says everyone in the reporter's organization on premium seats sees the same drop at the same time, which the reporter attributes to a change in how non-Fable usage is metered rather than to any change in workloads, prompts, repositories or plugins. (regression; 2 comments, 2 👍; +4 in the last 24h)

OpenCode

  • Release: v1.19.6 makes OpenCode 1 offer the upgrade to OpenCode 2.0 in the desktop app, which downloads in the background and installs only when you choose Restart to upgrade, Upgrade on quit, or Later, keeping your sessions, projects and settings; the release notes say plugins made for OpenCode 1 need an update. In the core, sessions with many images no longer send oversized requests — when a session's image history passes 25 MiB, the oldest images are replaced with a placeholder — and a provider error for a request body that is too large now starts compaction and a retry instead of failing the turn.
  • Release: Alongside it, process-daemon-v0.6.0 publishes opencode-pty 0.6.0 (protocol 9) from packages/process-daemon to npm as @opencode/pty@0.6.0.
  • News: OpenCode Browse — the Hacker News post describes Browse as letting OpenCode and other MCP clients use your real browser, where agents read, click, type, take screenshots, record tabs, and hand logins and 2FA back to you.

Oh My Pi

  • Release: Across v18.21.0–v18.22.0, binary analysis moves out of the standalone ida and ghidra tools into the backend-neutral dsm namespace (xd://eval/dsm), the ida.enabled, ida.maxOpen and ida.idleCloseSec settings are replaced by disassembler.backend, disassembler.maxOpen and disassembler.idleCloseSec, and the legacy standalone disassembler tools, the Copy and Edit-in-editor buttons in the Tern plan review sheet, plus PlanReviewOverlay options in their old form are removed — options now take PlanReviewOverlayChoice objects. The same range makes TtyWriter require a drain threshold and callback and only support independently reopenable TTYs, requires terminals with output backpressure to implement onOutputDrain(callback) returning an unsubscribe function, and reworks the AgentSession run lifecycle: agent_end is emitted once when a run can no longer resume, agent_pause reports runs stopped while awaiting work, hasPendingAsyncWork(), settleAsyncWork() and suppressAutoResumeUntilPrompt() are replaced by isRunActive, wakeSources and waitForRunEnd(), and abort() now also ends runs paused on background work.
  • Release: It fixes slow streaming of Gemma tool calls with large arguments, and fixes the xAI Grok OAuth model grok-composer-2.5-fast being identified as non-reasoning, so it now supports thinking levels from minimal through xhigh.
  • Release: It adds Tern plan review editing and comments — double-click a plan to edit it, select text to add Google Docs-style comments, and send comments to Refine — Ghidra support with automatic setup of Ghidra, JDK and PyGhidra when analysis is explicitly requested, with Auto mode using an installed IDA Pro when available and falling back to Ghidra otherwise, and sharing of live analysis databases with child agents through db.handle() and dsm.open(handle). Also added are configurable automatic subagent prewalk via task.agentPrewalkAuto, automatic reasoning-capability detection with remembered effort levels for unknown models, inline image and web-page replies with interactive embedded pages in Tern replies (tui.renderEmbeds to disable the rendering), and Modal as a hosted inference provider, while the local speech model changes from Kokoro to Phonon 31M.

jcode

  • Release: v1.0.0 reworks swarms to plan jobs in phases and parallel lanes, start workers automatically as dependencies finish, and show the whole team's progress in one pinned view, and it launches jcode Cloud, where /cloud moves a session or coordinated swarm to a VM, keeps it working after disconnecting, and /local brings the conversation and repository back.
  • Release: It adds full-conversation search in /resume with typo tolerance, live previews, and local and cloud sessions in the same picker; account priority tiers with hot-swap on Ctrl+Alt+J/K and refreshed /usage cards; per-session context limits; bounded JavaScript previews of live and completed codemode calls that survive status changes and transcript compaction; worker lane progress and final reports in completion messages; and live voice input with a waveform and streaming draft transcript.
  • Release: jcode says the terminal is lighter, with lower CPU usage, fewer background wakeups, faster transcript rendering and less rendered-text memory, citing a profiled release client at 25% less CPU, idle client wakeups down from 2.68 to 1.51 per second, and rendered-span memory in a large conversation down from 20.4 MB to 14.6 MB; it also says spinner-frame processing became 3.5 times faster and append-frame processing on a 4,000-message transcript 8.3 times faster, and that cloud sessions load recent history first and fetch older messages on demand, shrinking a 7,000-message session's initial history payload from 14.3 MB to 261 KB.

Hermes Agent

  • Release: v0.23.2 is described as a patch release rolling up the work since v0.23.1 into a stable release for the GitHub release (CLI and installers), the Microsoft Store app, Docker and Hermes Cloud, with full curated notes for the window deferred to v0.24.0. It fixes desktop chats created by an August build with a bare custom provider so they can send again after updating, makes a Desktop or TUI reply that streamed beside a todo or memory call settle instead of leaving the Stop button up, and stops a crash mid-stream on Telegram and other edit-streaming chats from showing a duplicate "Recovered reply".
  • Release: Hermes lists as included in this window, but undocumented here on purpose, durable subagents that survive a gateway restart or crash and can be continued on their own conversation, one prompt-cache clock per session, hermes fallback check for fallback-chain readiness, hermes update --force to stop gateways at once instead of draining, one-time browser_vault codes entered from Telegram and Discord, opt-in shared Telegram DM threads, the Gemini Interactions API by default for Gemini 3 and later plus Gemini 4 Carbon, fast mode for Claude Mythos 5.2, per-job cron options (wrap_response, a fresh thread per run), the plugin APIs ctx.fork_session, ctx.redact_text() and ctx.register_idle_task, and a slimmer macOS bundle that installs Chromium on first use.
  • Hot issue: #156670: an issue, filed as a feature request and tagged security, reports that on a multi-monitor Mac computer_use can still disrupt the human sharing the machine, because foreground fallback (delivery_mode: "foreground" / raise_window) brings the app to the front on whatever display it is on and posts real system-wide input that collides with the user's own mouse and keyboard — in --yolo / no-approval sessions with no prompt at all, about 30 foreground calls over two weeks in the reporter's local history — and because the agent works in whichever window is there, often on the display the user is actively using; it asks for foreground: ask as the default that survives --yolo and for an avoid_active_display setting that moves windows with AX. (type/security; 3 comments, 0 👍; +3 in the last 24h)

Weekly Diff 2026-11-16

⬛ Overview · 🟪 AI Agents · 🟦 AI Models & Labs · 🟧 AI Policy · 🟨 Data Engineering · ⬜ Weekly Diff · 🟫 Trends

Sources: 330 items the pages showed from 2026-11-10 to 2026-11-16 | Written by claude-opus-5-5 | Text in italics is interpretation | Generated: 22:30 UTC

Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2. Google made Gemini 4 Carbon available and introduced Gemini 4 Hydrogen. Azure Databricks set dates for model retirements and an MCP endpoint, and the European Commission adopted an implementing regulation on AI regulatory sandboxes.

Claude Fable 5.2 in coding agents

Claude Code v2.1.321 added Claude Fable 5.2 (claude-fable-5-2) as the default Fable model. It has 1M context and costs $8/$40 per Mtok, with $0.20/Mtok for cache reads. The same release fixed MCP OAuth requests that sent secrets such as refresh tokens to another host when a server redirected them. It separately fixed a case where a read-only Bash command ran outside the sandbox without a permission prompt.

Pi v1.5.1 also added Fable 5.2 to its anthropic provider. Its notes say that requests Fable 5.2's safety classifiers refuse before any output are answered by Claude Opus 5 through server-side fallback, and are billed at Opus 5's price. The same release changed the default model of that provider to Claude Opus 5.5.

Two issues describe friction with the new model and with later releases. One issue reports that DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 stops Claude Code from downloading feature flags, so the /model picker offers Fable 5.1 instead of 5.2. Another issue reports that 2.1.323 removed the subagentStatusLine setting. Its reporter calls the setting the only place to see each subagent's context, cost, model and effort. A Team subscriber reports that weekly usage reached 100% about 30 hours and 31 minutes after the reset on 2026-11-04. Later in the week, Claude Code v2.1.325 fixed a security issue in how zstd-compressed responses are decoded.

For teams whose clients require telemetry to be off, the reported link between DISABLE_TELEMETRY and the model picker is worth watching, because a privacy setting may hide the new default Fable model. Pi's note suggests that the cost of a Fable request can depend on whether the request is refused.

Azure Databricks dates and defaults

The Genie One MCP Beta endpoint reaches end of life on 2026-11-30, after which requests fail. The note points workloads to the system.ai.genie_one_mcp MCP in Unity Gateway. Gemini 3.6 Flash retires on 2026-11-19. From that date, calls are redirected to Gemini 3.8 Flash at the same price. Zhipu AI GLM 5.2 is deprecated and retires on 2027-02-04, with GLM 5.3 as the recommended replacement.

Starting on or after 2026-12-10, external access to Unity Catalog managed Delta tables will be available by default for eligible workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled. Smart Routing, which is in Beta, now routes only subagents. Databricks says it costs up to 70% less in internal benchmarks and cuts p90 routing latency from 9 seconds to 2 seconds. Smart Routing for Codex is paused.

Two tools changed how they handle an app's compute size. Terraform provider v1.143.0 now updates databricks_app through the asynchronous API. As a result, an omitted compute_size resets to MEDIUM, and an omitted git_source clears the app's default git source. Databricks CLI v1.26.0 no longer sends compute_size when a bundle does not declare it. A deploy therefore no longer resets a manually resized app to the default size.

The two tools now treat an undeclared app size in opposite ways, so apps managed with both may end up at different sizes depending on which tool deployed last. The compliance-profile change is worth watching, since access will then depend on metastore external data access settings and Unity Catalog privileges.

Gemini 4 models in BigQuery and agent catalogs

BigQuery generative AI functions now support gemini-4-carbon and gemini-4-hydrogen. The notes call each model generally available.

Oh My Pi's v18.18.8 catalog lists Gemini 4 Carbon at $2 input, $0.10 cached and $10 output per 1M tokens through 2026-11-30, then $4, $0.20 and $20. Its v18.20.1 lists Gemini 4 Hydrogen on Google Antigravity at $1.50/$7.50 per million tokens. The same release paused Google Antigravity again and points users to GEMINI_API_KEY with Google AI Studio or to the google-vertex provider. An earlier v18.18.4 had paused Antigravity because Google may restrict accounts that use it outside its own apps.

If that catalog's dates hold, Carbon's per-token prices double after 2026-11-30, so cost estimates made this month may not carry over to December. The repeated pausing in one tool suggests that Antigravity access through third-party agents is less settled than access through API keys or Vertex.

EU AI Act implementation

The Commission also published guidelines on the transparency obligations for certain AI systems under Article 50 of the AI Act on 2026-11-12. The AI Act timeline lists 2026-12-02 for two milestones: bans on sexual deepfakes and CSAM generators, and the end of the Article 50(2) transition. In the Netherlands, a motion by El Boujdaini and others concerns equipping authorities sufficiently for supervision of the AI Act.

The Article 50 guidelines appeared 20 days before the Article 50(2) transition ends, which leaves a short window for clients whose AI systems fall under that article to compare their practice with them.

Agent tool usage

Several agent tools moved sharply in OpenRouter's app ranking. Kilo Code was week #5 with 7.03T tokens/week, +46% vs previous week. Strix was week #9 with 2.56T tokens/week, +45% vs previous week. OpenClaw was week #8 with 2.69T tokens/week, -46% vs previous week. omp was week #11 with 2.13T tokens/week, -36% vs previous week, while its npm package had 295,519 downloads/week, +34% vs previous week. Hermes Agent was week #3 with 13.02T tokens/week (+5.1% vs previous week), and Claude Code was week #4 with 10.80T tokens/week (+7.5% vs previous week).

Among models on 2026-11-15, deepseek-v4.1-flash-20261017 led OpenRouter tokens with 59.23T. tencent/hy4-20261104 was #2 with 18.12T, after ranking #4 last week.

omp's OpenRouter tokens and npm downloads moved in opposite directions, which suggests OpenRouter tokens alone may not track how much a tool is used. Swings near 46% in both directions show one week's movement, not a lasting shift.
